svg.title: Five ideas I keep coming back to
svg.desc: 1. Separate content from presentation. Editors deserve a structured studio; users deserve static-site speed. Decoupling the CMS from the frontend is how you get both, and it's the single decision that has paid off most often in my career. 2. Measure before you optimise. Core Web Vitals in CI, Search Console on a dashboard, real-user data over lab scores. A rewrite without a baseline is a guess with a budget. 3. SEO and tracking are engineering. Redirect maps, structured data, canonical URLs and analytics events belong in the ticket and the code review, not in a plugin installed the week after launch. 4. Boring infrastructure, interesting products. Postgres, a CDN, one CI pipeline and a typed codebase cover a remarkable amount of ground. Spend novelty where the product actually needs it. 5. Lead by staying hands-on. The best architecture reviews come from people who still ship. I keep most of my week in the codebase so the team's standards are ones I live by, not ones I remember. “Problem-solving over syntax. Culture over raw output.” — HOW I RUN A TEAM
